question.problem: Find the range of the function $f(x)=-\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})+4.$
question.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ consists of two intervals:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡x\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty )
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty ).
$$

We can split this into two inequalities:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})\le -1,\,\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})\ge 1
$$

To find the range of $f(x),$ we consider both intervals separately.

- Multiplying the first interval by $-1$ and adding $4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})\le -1 \\  & -\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})\ge 1 \\  & -\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})+4\ge 1+4 \\  & f(x)\ge 5.\end{aligned}
$$

- Multiplying the second interval by $-1$ and adding $4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})\ge 1 \\  & -\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})\le -1 \\  & -\operatorname{csc}⁡(4x-\frac{\pi }{3})+4\le -1+4 \\  & f(x)\le 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining both inequalities, we get

$$
f(x)\ge 5,\,f(x)\le 3.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the range is $f(x)\in (-\infty ,3]\cup [5,\infty ).$
